content_voiceover: This flowchart summarizes the full treatment algorithm for confirmed acute promyelocytic leukemia. Diagnosis is confirmed with peripheral blood and bone marrow karyotype, FISH, and RT-PCR for t fifteen;seventeen, PML dash RARA, and its fusion variants. For induction, low or intermediate risk patients receive ATRA plus arsenic trioxide, or ATRA plus chemotherapy if arsenic isn't available, while high risk patients add gemtuzumab ozogamicin or idarubicin to ATRA plus ATO. Throughout induction, clinicians must watch for differentiation syndrome, treated with steroid prophylaxis and dexamethasone, monitor for ATO related QT prolongation by keeping potassium above four and magnesium above one point eight with twice weekly EKGs, watch for fluid overload, and consider CNS prophylaxis in high risk patients or those with prior CNS hemorrhage. A bone marrow assessment at week four should show blasts below five percent before moving to consolidation. After consolidation, RT-PCR on peripheral blood determines the monitoring path: if negative, low and intermediate risk patients get CBC surveillance without routine molecular monitoring, while high risk patients get CBC and RT-PCR every three months with consideration of maintenance therapy. If RT-PCR is positive, confirmed relapse triggers salvage with ATRA plus chemotherapy, arsenic trioxide plus gemtuzumab, and consideration of hematopoietic stem cell transplant.
keypoints: Induction: ATRA plus ATO for low/intermediate risk; add GO or idarubicin for high risk
Watch for differentiation syndrome, ATO-related QT prolongation, and fluid overload
BM assessment at week four; consolidation continues until blasts less than five percent
Post-consolidation RT-PCR guides monitoring: negative goes to surveillance, positive triggers relapse management
Relapse treatment includes ATRA/chemo, ATO plus GO, and consideration of HSCT
keypoint_voiceover: APL treatment: ATRA plus arsenic trioxide for low and intermediate risk, adding gemtuzumab or idarubicin for high risk, with vigilance for differentiation syndrome and QT prolongation. After consolidation, RT-PCR determines whether patients go to routine surveillance or are managed as relapse with salvage therapy and possible transplant.
